_meta.indication: Treatment of premenopausal women with acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD), characterized by low sexual desire causing marked distress or interpersonal difficulty; not indicated in postmenopausal women or in men, or to enhance sexual performance.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of BMT 1.75 mg SC vs. placebo, 6 months
pivotal_trials.population: Premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD (with or without decreased arousal)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Coprimary endpoints: change from baseline to EOS in sexual desire (FSFI-D) and in distress from low desire (FSDS-DAO Q13)
pivotal_trials.result: FSFI-D median change +0.6 (BMT) vs 0 (PBO), mean difference 0.30, p<0.001; FSDS-DAO Q13 distress median change -1 (BMT) vs 0 (PBO), mean difference -0.37, p<0.001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>4%): nausea (40.0% vs 1.3% placebo), flushing (20.3% vs 0.3%), injection site reactions (13.2% vs 8.4%), headache (11.3% vs 1.9%), and vomiting (4.8% vs 0.2%). Discontinuation due to adverse reactions was 18% (BMT) vs 2% (placebo). Warnings include transient blood pressure increase/heart rate reduction and focal hyperpigmentation.
target_moa: Bremelanotide is a synthetic heptapeptide melanocortin receptor (MCR) agonist; a nonselective high-affinity agonist for melanocortin receptors, with MC4R (expressed on CNS neurons) mediating relevant sexual-function activity.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise issues requiring external expert advice.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) review NDA 210557 for bremelanotide (Vyleesi), received March 23, 2018 and approved June 21, 2019 for premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD; no advisory committee was convened.
